extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, academic researchers, and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed standards for sustaining and improving the academic peer-review ecosystem, covering reviewer incentives, transparency models, quality metrics, editorial responsibilities, training, and technological innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer workload and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Many academics are asked to provide several reviews every week, often with tight deadlines; the system over-relies on a small pool of academics who respond and accept requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid concentrating requests on the same cooperative volunteers; recognize that reviewers commonly do reviews in evenings/weekends, which contributes to fatigue, delayed turnaround times, and incomplete assessments. Consider systems to distribute requests more equitably and limit overload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and incentives for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of formal recognition or reward for reviewers' contributions is a major concern; listing reviews on ORCID or Web of Science adds little career value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce incentives — non-financial (discounts on publication fees, free access, continuing medical education credits, public acknowledgement) and/or financial (redirecting part of publishers' revenues back to reviewers or institutions) — to retain reviewers, support career advancement, and improve job satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification and public metrics of review activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for a global platform to quantify reviewer activities and provide tools to evaluate the quality and relevance of reviews based on factors such as quality, timeliness and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create publicly accessible metrics; editors should rate reviews for thoroughness and actionable insights. The platform should incentivise and enhance review quality fairly and sustainably, though appointing more editors may be required to implement such evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality: thoroughness and actionable insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be thorough and provide actionable insights that enhance rigour and quality of academic work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors play a central role in evaluating and rating reviews for thoroughness and usefulness. Metrics and recognition schemes should prioritise depth and constructiveness over cursory or perfunctory feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Prolonged turnaround times undermine the peer-review process; reviewers often juggle heavy workloads and personal commitments leading to delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentivise timely completion of reviews through recognition, metrics, or rewards. Consider realistic deadlines and support mechanisms to avoid rushed, incomplete assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and number of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, each manuscript is evaluated by two or more independent reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain multiple independent assessments to reduce bias and improve detection of critical flaws. Explore models (pre- and post-publication) that encourage broader engagement while guarding independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency vs anonymity (open peer review tradeoffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review (disclosing reviewers' identities) increases transparency but can limit what reviewers are willing to write and may create bias or collusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh benefits of transparency against risks: withholding legitimate criticism to avoid offence, inappropriately positive reviews for reciprocal benefit, and potential for disputes among colleagues. Design open-review policies with safeguards to minimise bias and protect frank critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-publication review models
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting pre- and post-publication review that encourages multiple reviewers to engage in discussions (including on social media) could accelerate dissemination and provide ongoing feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize benefits (faster dissemination, continuous feedback) and risks (subjective or uninformed comments, potential discreditation). Implement moderation, verification, and reputation mechanisms if opening commentary channels widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for data verification and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-review reforms should enforce better standards for data verification and methodology to preserve research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise checks on data quality and methodological rigor during review; incorporate tools, checklists, or specialist reviewers for data/method verification to reduce likelihood of flawed published work and retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technological innovations including artificial intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporating technological innovations, including AI, could help create a more modern, efficient, and sustainable peer-review ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore AI tools to assist screening, detect anomalies, or support reviewers, while being mindful of limitations and risks. Technology should augment, not replace, expert judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial resourcing and role in ensuring quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors would need to play a central role in evaluating reviews and rating them; many editors receive modest stipends or work voluntarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider appointing more editors or providing better resourcing/stipends to enable rigorous oversight, review rating, and implementation of incentive systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational activities and mentorship (e.g., pairing junior mentees with senior mentors, didactic sessions, editorial board participation) can nurture the next generation of reviewers and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create reviewer mentorship programmes, training modules, and apprenticeship schemes; recognise outstanding reviewers with promotions or editorial opportunities to develop skills and sustain reviewer pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias, collusion, and conflicts in review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Open review and current selection practices can create bias (withholding criticism, reciprocal positive reviews) and potential for collusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement conflict-of-interest disclosures, selection diversity, and monitoring to detect patterns of reciprocal favour or collusion. Balance transparency with protections to preserve candour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and career value of reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing review activity on platforms adds little value to careers; the system disproportionately benefits publishers financially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop credentialing or metrics that meaningfully contribute to career advancement (e.g., institutional recognition, counting towards promotion), and consider redistributing some publishing revenues to support reviewers or institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability of the peer-review ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising reviewers' time and expertise is essential for sustaining the academic publishing ecosystem and advancing public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt systemic reforms (incentives, training, resourcing, technology) to retain reviewers, improve review quality, and ensure the long-term viability of peer review as a cornerstone of scholarly communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for authors expressing unconventional ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should allow authors to express ideas that challenge convention while maintaining rigorous standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure review policies and editorial judgment protect legitimate novel or contrarian contributions from undue suppression, by focusing critiques on methodology and evidence rather than conformity to prevailing views.
